newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Paper completes ANM buy.
newsitem.headline: FCL Paper completes ANM buy.

text.p: New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Paper Ltd said on Monday it had completed its purchase of the remaining 50 percent of Australian Newsprint Mills from the News Limited Group.
It said the total consideration for the deal was A$293.5 million, paid half in cash and half via a capital note.
ANM, Australia's only producer of newsprint and groundwood specialty papers, is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of Fletcher Challenge Paper. Fletcher has held a 50 percent stake in ANM since 1988.
An initial payment of A$263.5 million will be made, with the balance made up through the A$30 million capital note, payable over the next six years.
Fletcher Challenge Paper chief executive John Hood said the purchase would solidify Fletcher Challenge Paper's position as the pre-eminent publications paper supplier in Australasia.

"ANM has been a very solid performer in recent years, in what has been a difficult era for paper manufacturers. Its strong customer relationships and its commitment to product quality and innovation are important competitive advantages," Hood said.
The company has long-term contractual arrangements for supply of newsprint to Australian newspaper publishers, including the News Limited group.
Fletcher Paper said ANM supplied approximately 60 percent of Australia's annual newsprint and specialty papers needs.
It has two mills -- Boyer in Tasmania and Albury in NSW -- with combined newsprint and specialty papers capacity of 500,000 tonnes per year.

ANM operates a recycled fibre plant at Albury, completed in 1995 at a cost of A$133 million, that uses 165,000 tonnes of waste paper per year and enables it to produce newsprint with recycled content of 40 percent at Albury and 20 percent at Boyer.
In addition, ANM has 31,000 hectares of plantation forests which are being developed as part of long-term strategy to further reduce fibre costs.
At present, 58 percent of the fibre for the mills is sourced from established forests under long-term agreements with the state governments of Tasmania, NSW and Victoria.
The Australian Competition & Consumer Commission recently said it would not intervene in the ANM buy.
